title: Automatic rollback orchestration using cohort-based quality gates for config and model diffs
creator: Jordan Li
description:
Goal: Implement a controller that performs automatic rollback orchestration driven by cohort-based quality gates for any deployment that changes model or serving config (quantization, batch settings, KV cache toggles, kernel/compile flags, model version). This is intended to complement existing canary/A-B flows by fusing multiple signal sources (quality evals, latency/PU, error spikes) and making a best-effort automated revert decision within a short window so customer-facing regressions are minimized.

Scope:
- Evaluate on both model version swaps and operational config diffs (e.g., quantize->int8, cache hotfix, kernel selection).
- Support: canary (small % traffic) and A/B (traffic split) patterns.
- Controller will consume: cohort eval results (batch evals + streaming metrics), real-time latency/95/99 metrics, error rate (5xx), token-accuracy style metrics from eval harnesses, and custom customer probes.
- Rollback policy language: declarative policy objects (thresholds, weight, fuse-window, cooldown, allowed-fallbacks).

Design decisions / trade-offs considered: 
1) Centralized policy engine vs per-cluster controllers: we will implement a centralized policy engine that emits rollback decisions and per-cluster agents apply changes. Centralization reduces policy drift and helps audit, at cost of additional control-plane latency.
2) Time-window for eval signal: use a sliding window (configurable, default 5m with min 3m) to reduce transient noise, but keep short to limit customer exposure.
3) Signal fusion strategy: weighted heuristics (quality evals > functional customer metrics > latency). Quality regressions from evals can trigger immediate pause; severe production errors (5xx surge) will preempt ev al signals and cause instantaneous rollback.
4) Canary sizing: recommend initial canary at 1% traffic across 3 randomized cohorts (geo/tenant/usage) to surface heterogenous regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Controller can read a policy and evaluate live signals and stored cohort eval results.
- For a model/config change with a deliberately injected quality regression, the controller detects regression within policy window and returns traffic to previous variant automatically.
- Audit trail: each automated decision must be logged with reason, contributing signals, and a link to the alert/dashboard.
- Operators can opt into auto-rollback or manual-review mode per project.

Implementation plan (phases):
Phase 1 (2 sprints): Policy schema + lightweight controller prototype. Ingests existing eval results (from evals service) and production metrics from metrics pipeline, performs rule evaluation, emits decision events to rollout service.
Phase 2 (2 sprints): Per-cluster agents and rollout actuator integration. Add canary cohort selection API, traffic split enforcement, and safe-fallback selection logic (e.g., compatible model variant or previous pinned rollout).
Phase 3 (1 sprint): Observability + dashboard tiles (per-rollout traces, contributing signal breakdown), incident playbooks, and customer-facing opt-in toggle in Console.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for policy evaluation and decision scoring.
- Integration tests using synthetic workloads (latency/error injection) and synthetic eval datasets to simulate quality regressions.
- Chaos tests: ensure controller behaves when metrics lag or eval service is unavailable (fallback to conservative manual-stop + alert).

Operational concerns:
- Ensure controller respects per-customer isolation and RBAC; changes must be audited.
- Rate-limit automated rollbacks to avoid thundering reverts; require cooldown and escalation if repeated regressions occur.

comments: 2026-02-20 - Jordan Li: Created ticket with initial problem statement and goals. Spiked controller prototype to validate ingest of cohort evals. Linked PR and Confluence PRD.
2026-02-25 - Mateo Singh: Completed spike showing we can ingest 1-min cohort eval blobs and map to rollout IDs. Observed ~20s processing latency in prototype; likely fine but needs optimization.

2026-03-02 - Evie Martin (review): Reviewed policy schema draft. Requested explicit fields for signal provenance and confidence scores. Raised concern about central control-plane availability affecting rollouts; suggested fallback local evaluation.

2026-03-04 - Mateo Singh: Added 'signal_provenance' and 'confidence' fields to schema. Implemented emergency fallback: if policy engine unreachable, agents will pause new rollouts and send an alert to on-call.
2026-03-08 - QA: Added integration test cases for intentional quality degradation in canary cohorts. Found race condition with traffic-split update API when quick successive rollbacks occur.
2026-03-10 - Mateo Singh: Fixed race by serializing rollout operations per-service; added 30s cooldown default. Deployed controller to staging for end-to-end validation.
2026-03-12 - Security (note): Confirmed no sensitive data flows outside metrics plane; no immediate security blockers but recommended audit of logged eval payloads to avoid PII leaks.
